sections.h2: Where is the Guilford County Register of Deeds and when is it open?
sections.html:
The office runs two locations: 201 W. Market St. in Greensboro, where real estate and recording sit on the second floor, and 325 E. Russell Ave., Room 155, in High Point. The phone line for both is 336-641-7556, and the hours are Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

Mail for recording goes to P.O. Box 3427, Greensboro, NC 27402, or to P.O. Box 1467, High Point, NC 27261. The county was set up in 1771 from parts of Rowan and Orange, and records for a house in Jamestown, Summerfield or Gibsonville land in the same index as a downtown Greensboro condo, because the register keeps one set of land records for the whole county.

The Census Bureau estimated 562,234 residents in July 2025. Email guilforddeeds@guilfordcountync.gov for general questions.

sections.h2: How do you record a deed in Guilford County?
sections.html:
Bring or send a standard-format deed, pay the recording fee and the excise tax, and the office records it. You can also submit it electronically, because the Register of Deeds accepts all electronically submitted real estate documents through approved vendors.

Electronic filing returns the recording data and a stamped image within minutes, and the system reports right away if the document fails the North Carolina Real Estate Recording Standards. A paper document must give the name and address of the person to receive it back after recording. The county lists what makes a document standard:

  • 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 paper, printed on one side in black on white.
  • A 3 inch blank margin at the top of page one and at least a quarter inch on the other sides.
  • A legible font no smaller than 9 point, with the instrument type stated at the top of the first page.
  • Pen is allowed for filling blanks and for corrections.

Miss any one of those and the non-standard document fee is added to the usual recording fee. Knowing those limits tells you what the office will and will not do with your paperwork.

sections.h2: What does the Guilford County Register of Deeds charge?
sections.html:
A general instrument costs $26 for the first 15 pages and a mortgage or deed of trust costs $64 for the first 35 pages, each with $4 for every added page. These match the uniform statewide schedule, and the county's own table adds the smaller items.

Guilford County Register of Deeds fee schedule, recording and copies
ItemFee printed by the county
Deed or other instrument$26 first 15 pages, $4 each added page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64 first 35 pages, $4 each added page
Non-standard document$25 on top of the recording fee
Each added instrument in one document$10
Satisfaction of security instrumentNo fee
Plat or condominium map recording$21 per page
Certified copy$5 first page, $2 each added page

Source: the county's Recording and Real Estate page. Plain photocopies of real estate documents cost 5 cents a page in the office and $1 a page by mail. State law calls the statutory fees complete and exclusive and requires payment before filing.

sections.h2: Who pays the excise tax on a Guilford County deed?
sections.html:
The seller pays it, to the register of deeds, before the deed is recorded. The statute sets it at $1 on each $500 of the price or fraction of $500, and the county's table writes the same rate as $2 per thousand for deeds since August 1, 1991.

The county keeps half of the collection in its general fund and sends the rest to the state Department of Revenue each month. The tax is separate from the recording fee, so a closing statement shows both. The county page also shows older rates for deeds recorded between 1968 and July 1991, which you will see only when reading an old instrument. For a transaction on a house you plan to sell, ask the closing attorney for the final amount instead of estimating it from the sale price.

sections.h2: Why does recording order matter for a Guilford County sale?
sections.html:
In North Carolina a deed, option, or lease of more than three years does not bind lien creditors or later buyers for value until it is registered in the county where the land lies. Priority follows the order and time of registration.

Under that rule, an old loan that was paid off still shadows the title until a satisfaction is recorded. The county lists three routes to record one, and none carries a fee:

  • A satisfaction signed by the secured creditor and notarized.
  • A trustee's or substitute trustee's satisfaction of the deed of trust.
  • An affidavit of satisfaction prepared by a North Carolina attorney acting as a satisfaction agent when a lender fails to provide one.

The office no longer accepts the original deed of trust and note as proof of payoff. If a loan from a previous owner still shows open on your parcel, a recorded satisfaction clears the record, and your own attorney or the lender can help get it.

sections.h2: How can Guilford County owners guard against deed fraud?
sections.html:
Sign up for the county's Property Fraud Alert, which sends a notice when a document is recorded under a name variation you supplied. The Register of Deeds must record any document that meets legal requirements once fees and taxes are paid, and it does not verify whether the signature is genuine.

The county warns that owners of vacant or already-distressed properties, older homeowners and low-income homeowners are common targets. Warning signs it lists include a recorded transfer you never signed, property tax bills that stop arriving, and a notice of default when you own the home free and clear. A homeowner who finds a bad deed should gather the paperwork and report it to the Sheriff's Office or the Greensboro or High Point police, the District Attorney, a real estate attorney, and the Register of Deeds. The register has no authority to remove a recorded document, so ask a real estate attorney how to challenge it.

The same page recommends verifying credentials, reading contracts, and considering a title search and title insurance before any sale.

sections.h2: Can the Guilford County register fix an error in a recorded deed?
sections.html:
The register can correct how a document was indexed, but it cannot change what the document says. Under G.S. 132-1.10 the office records an instrument as presented and never alters the text, so a misspelled name, a defective legal description or a wrong loan amount needs a corrective instrument.

The Indexing Correction Request form covers indexing mistakes only. Questions go to 336-641-7556 or the office email. If the problem is in the deed itself, your attorney prepares the correction, and it is recorded under the same fee schedule as any other instrument.

The county's recording page also carries a Personal Information Redaction section and a Real Estate Document Request form for copies.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Guilford County homes?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists 246,403 housing units in July 2025 and a median owner-occupied value of $259,900 for 2020 to 2024. Owners occupy 59.9% of homes, and median gross rent is $1,163.

Median household income is $68,642 in 2024 dollars, and 2,876 building permits were issued in 2025. Of residents age one and older, 85.1% lived in the same house a year earlier. For the tax side of a sale, read our Guilford County property tax guide.

faqs.q: What is the phone number for the Guilford County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: 336-641-7556 for both the Greensboro and High Point offices. The Greensboro office is at 201 W. Market St. and the High Point office is at 325 E. Russell Ave., Room 155. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Guilford County?
faqs.a: A general instrument is $26 for the first 15 pages plus $4 for each added page, and a non-standard document adds $25. The deed excise tax is separate and is paid by the seller before recording.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed electronically in Guilford County?
faqs.a: Yes. The office accepts all electronically submitted real estate documents through its approved vendors, returns the recording information and stamped image within minutes, and flags documents that miss the state recording standards.

faqs.q: Does the Guilford County register check that a deed is real?
faqs.a: No. The office records any document that meets the legal format once fees and taxes are paid and does not judge its authenticity. Owners can enroll in the free Property Fraud Alert and report forged deeds to law enforcement and the District Attorney.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to record a satisfaction of a mortgage in Guilford County?
faqs.a: No. Satisfactions of security instruments, affidavits of satisfaction and trustee's satisfactions carry no recording fee. The office will not accept the original deed of trust and note as a substitute.
